japanese.breakfast.edamame-egg-soy-bowl.name: Edamame & Egg Soy Bowl on Brown Rice
components: Primary: Edamame and a soft-boiled egg on brown rice (45 g uncooked) with ginger-soy and sesame oil
Cucumber slices, spring onion and shredded nori
Green tea
steps: Cook the brown rice with 1.5 times its volume of water, about 30 minutes.
Boil the edamame 4 minutes, drain and pop the beans from the pods. Soft-boil the egg 6.5 minutes, cool and peel.
Mix the soy, sesame oil and grated ginger for the dressing.
Pile the edamame on the rice, halve the egg on top, spoon over the dressing and scatter with toasted sesame, sliced cucumber, spring onion and shredded nori.
Serve with a cup of green tea.
japanese.breakfast.edamame-egg-soy-bowl.source: A Japanese-style home breakfast bowl in place of natto gohan

japanese.breakfast.grilled-salmon-daikon.name: Grilled Salmon with Daikon & Brown Rice
components: Primary: 80 g grilled salted salmon (shiozake) with grilled shiitake
Small bowl brown rice (40 g uncooked)
Grated daikon and wakame with rice vinegar and soy
Bok choy ohitashi with bonito flakes and sesame
Green tea
steps: Cook the brown rice with 1.5 times its volume of water, about 30 minutes.
Salt the salmon lightly and rest 10 minutes; grill or pan-grill skin side down 5 minutes, turn and give it 3 minutes more, with the whole shiitake alongside.
Soak the wakame 3 minutes, squeeze, and mix with the grated daikon, rice vinegar and half the soy.
Blanch the bok choy 1 minute, squeeze, cut into 3 cm pieces and dress with the remaining soy; top with bonito flakes and toasted sesame.
Serve the salmon and shiitake with the rice, the daikon-wakame, the bok choy, sliced spring onion and a cup of green tea.
japanese.breakfast.grilled-salmon-daikon.source: Adapted from the traditional shiozake breakfast

japanese.breakfast.iri-dofu.name: Iri Dofu with Brown Rice
japanese.breakfast.iri-dofu.basedOn: Iri dofu, the Japanese home-style scrambled tofu with carrot, shiitake and egg, seasoned with soy and a little mirin.
components: Primary: 1 bowl iri dofu (tofu scramble with carrot, shiitake, edamame and egg)
Small bowl brown rice (40 g uncooked)
Green tea
steps: Cook the brown rice with 1.5 times its volume of water, about 30 minutes.
Press the tofu between paper towels for 5 minutes, then crumble it. Dice the carrot finely and slice the shiitake; thaw the edamame in hot water.
Heat the sesame oil in a non-stick pan, cook the carrot and shiitake 3 minutes, then add the crumbled tofu and stir over medium-high heat until the moisture cooks off.
Season with the soy and mirin, add the edamame, then pour the beaten egg over and stir until just set.
Serve over the rice with sliced spring onion and a cup of green tea.
japanese.breakfast.iri-dofu.source: Adapted from the traditional iri dofu

japanese.breakfast.oats-banana-walnuts.name: Oats with Yoghurt, Banana, Walnuts & Black Sesame
components: Primary: 1 bowl rolled oats (35 g) cooked in water, stirred with low-fat yoghurt
Half a banana, walnuts and toasted black sesame on top
Green tea
steps: Simmer the oats in 200 ml water with a pinch of salt for 5-6 minutes until thick; cool 2 minutes.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan 1 minute until they pop; roughly crush.
Stir the yoghurt through the oats, top with sliced banana, broken walnuts and the sesame.
Serve with a cup of green tea.
japanese.breakfast.oats-banana-walnuts.source: A Western-Japanese home breakfast (yoghurt oats with kuro goma)

japanese.breakfast.saba-shioyaki-set.name: Saba Shioyaki Breakfast Set
japanese.breakfast.saba-shioyaki-set.basedOn: Saba shioyaki teishoku, the classic Japanese breakfast set of grilled salted mackerel with rice, miso soup and a small vegetable side.
components: Primary: 1 piece grilled salted mackerel (saba shioyaki) with grated daikon
Small bowl brown rice (40 g uncooked)
Miso soup with wakame and spring onion
Spinach ohitashi with sesame
Green tea
steps: Rinse the brown rice and cook it with 1.5 times its volume of water (about 30 minutes, or in the rice cooker).
Make dashi: steep the kombu in 300 ml water, bring almost to the boil, remove the kombu, add the bonito flakes, rest 2 minutes and strain.
Salt the mackerel lightly on both sides and rest 10 minutes; grill or pan-grill skin side first, 4-5 minutes a side, until the skin blisters.
Blanch the spinach 40 seconds, squeeze dry, cut into 3 cm lengths and dress with half the soy and 2 tablespoons of dashi; top with toasted sesame.
Soak the wakame in the remaining dashi for 3 minutes, warm gently and dissolve the miso off the heat; add sliced spring onion.
Serve the mackerel with grated daikon and the rest of the soy, alongside the rice, soup, spinach and a cup of green tea.
japanese.breakfast.saba-shioyaki-set.source: Adapted from the traditional saba shioyaki teishoku

japanese.breakfast.salmon-onigiri-miso-s.name: Salmon Onigiri with Miso Soup
japanese.breakfast.salmon-onigiri-miso-s.basedOn: Sake onigiri, the Japanese rice ball filled with flaked grilled salmon and wrapped in nori, here made with brown rice.
components: Primary: 2 brown-rice onigiri (50 g uncooked) filled with flaked baked salmon, wrapped in nori
Miso soup with wakame and spinach
Green tea
steps: Cook the brown rice with 1.5 times its volume of water until tender and slightly sticky, about 30 minutes; keep warm.
Salt the salmon and bake or pan-grill 8 minutes; flake with a fork, discarding the skin.
Make dashi from the kombu and bonito in 300 ml water; strain.
With wet, lightly salted hands, shape the warm rice into two triangles, pressing a spoon of salmon into the centre of each; roll the edges in toasted sesame and wrap a half sheet of nori around each.
Soak the wakame in the dashi, add the chopped spinach and warm 1 minute; dissolve the miso off the heat and add spring onion.
Serve the onigiri with the soup and a cup of green tea.
japanese.breakfast.salmon-onigiri-miso-s.source: Adapted from the traditional sake onigiri

japanese.breakfast.sweet-potato-egg-miso.name: Steamed Sweet Potato with Boiled Egg & Miso Soup
components: Primary: Half a steamed sweet potato (satsumaimo style) with 1 boiled egg
Miso soup with tofu, wakame and spring onion
Edamame with toasted sesame
Green tea
steps: Scrub the sweet potato and steam the half, skin on, 15-18 minutes until a skewer slides in; cut into thick rounds and sprinkle with a little salt.
Boil the egg 9 minutes, cool under the tap, peel and halve. Boil the edamame 4 minutes in the same pot.
Make dashi from the kombu and bonito in 300 ml water; add the cubed tofu and wakame, warm 2 minutes, dissolve the miso off the heat and add spring onion.
Serve the sweet potato and egg with the soup, the edamame tossed with toasted sesame, and a cup of green tea.
japanese.breakfast.sweet-potato-egg-miso.source: Japanese home breakfast of mushi-imo (steamed sweet potato) with miso soup

japanese.dinner.agedashi-tofu.name: Agedashi-Style Tofu in Dashi Sauce with Spinach & Brown Rice
japanese.dinner.agedashi-tofu.basedOn: Agedashi dofu, fried tofu in a hot dashi-soy sauce with grated daikon and ginger, a Japanese izakaya and home classic; here pan-fried in a teaspoon of oil.
components: Primary: 150 g pan-crisped tofu in dashi-soy sauce with shiitake, grated daikon and ginger
Spinach ohitashi
Small bowl brown rice (45 g uncooked)
steps: Cook the brown rice (45 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).
Press the tofu between paper towels under a plate for 10 minutes and cut into 4 thick blocks.
Make 150 ml dashi with the kombu and bonito flakes; add the soy and the sliced shiitake and simmer 3 minutes.
Heat the rice bran oil in a non-stick pan and fry the tofu blocks over medium-high heat 3 minutes a side until golden and crisp-edged.
Blanch the spinach 30 seconds, squeeze and cut; dress with a spoonful of the dashi sauce.
Set the tofu in bowls, pour the hot shiitake sauce around, top with grated daikon, grated ginger and spring onion. Serve with the spinach and the small bowl of rice.
japanese.dinner.agedashi-tofu.source: Adapted from the traditional agedashi dofu, pan-fried rather than deep-fried and without mirin

japanese.dinner.chawanmushi.name: Chawanmushi (Savoury Egg Custard with Prawn & Shiitake) with Greens & Brown Rice
components: Primary: 2-egg chawanmushi steamed with dashi, prawns and shiitake
French beans and spinach with sesame
Edamame, 50 g
Small bowl brown rice (45 g uncooked)
steps: Cook the brown rice (45 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).
Make 200 ml dashi with the kombu and bonito flakes and let it cool to warm; season with the soy and salt.
Beat the eggs gently, stir in the dashi (about 2.5 parts dashi to 1 part egg) and strain through a sieve.
Put the peeled prawns and sliced shiitake into two cups or ramekins, pour in the egg mixture and cover with foil.
Steam over gently simmering water 12-15 minutes until just set; a skewer should come out clean. Rest 2 minutes.
Blanch the french beans and edamame 3 minutes, and the spinach 30 seconds; dress the beans and spinach with toasted sesame. Serve with the small bowl of rice.

japanese.dinner.grilled-salmon-daikon.name: Grilled Salmon with Grated Daikon, Miso Soup & Brown Rice
japanese.dinner.grilled-salmon-daikon.basedOn: Shake no shioyaki, salt-grilled salmon served with grated daikon, miso soup and rice, the archetypal Japanese home dinner.
components: Primary: 110 g salt-grilled salmon with grated daikon, lemon and soy
Miso soup with wakame and spring onion
Spinach ohitashi with sesame
Small bowl brown rice (45 g uncooked)
steps: Cook the brown rice (45 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).
Salt the salmon on both sides and leave 10 minutes; pat dry.
Make 200 ml dashi with the kombu and bonito flakes; add the soaked wakame, dissolve the miso in off the boil and finish with sliced spring onion.
Blanch the spinach 30 seconds, squeeze, cut into lengths and dress with a few drops of the soy and the toasted sesame seeds.
Grill the salmon skin side up under a hot grill 5 minutes, turn and grill 3 minutes, or pan-grill in a dry non-stick pan.
Serve with a mound of grated daikon, a lemon wedge and the remaining soy to drizzle; soup and spinach first, rice last.
japanese.dinner.grilled-salmon-daikon.source: Adapted from the traditional shake no shioyaki teishoku

japanese.dinner.kinpira-mackerel.name: Grilled Mackerel with Kinpira (Carrot & Daikon Stir-Fry), Miso Soup & Brown Rice
japanese.dinner.kinpira-mackerel.kidNote: Add the chilli flakes to the kinpira after setting the child's portion aside.
components: Primary: 1 salt-grilled mackerel with lemon
Kinpira of carrot, daikon and french beans with sesame oil, soy and chilli
Miso soup with wakame and spring onion
Small bowl brown rice (40 g uncooked)
steps: Cook the brown rice (40 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).
Clean and butterfly or fillet the mackerel, salt both sides and leave 10 minutes; pat dry.

Cut the carrot and daikon into thin matchsticks and the french beans into 3 cm pieces. Heat the sesame oil, stir-fry the vegetables 4 minutes, add the soy and 2 tablespoons water and cook until dry and glossy; finish with the chilli flakes.
Bring 200 ml water with the soaked wakame to a simmer, dissolve the miso in off the boil and add the spring onion.
Grill the mackerel skin side up under a hot grill 5 minutes, turn and grill 3-4 minutes until the skin blisters.
Serve the soup and kinpira first, the fish with a lemon wedge, and the small bowl of rice last.
japanese.dinner.kinpira-mackerel.source: Adapted from the traditional saba shioyaki with kinpira, without the usual sugar and mirin

japanese.dinner.nasu-dengaku.name: Nasu Dengaku (Miso-Glazed Eggplant) with Seared Tofu & Brown Rice
components: Primary: 150 g eggplant grilled with miso-mirin glaze and sesame, and 120 g seared tofu
Spinach ohitashi with bonito
Small bowl brown rice (45 g uncooked)
steps: Cook the brown rice (45 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).
Halve the eggplant lengthwise, score the flesh in a diamond pattern, brush with the sesame oil and grill or bake at 220 C for 15 minutes until soft.
Mix the miso with the mirin and 1 teaspoon water, spread over the eggplant and grill 3 minutes more until bubbling; scatter the sesame seeds.
Press the tofu, cut into two slabs and sear in the dry non-stick pan (the eggplant's oil is enough) 4 minutes a side; top with grated ginger.
Blanch the spinach 30 seconds, squeeze, cut and dress with the soy and bonito flakes.
Serve the spinach first, then the eggplant and tofu, with the small bowl of rice.
japanese.dinner.nasu-dengaku.source: Adapted from the traditional nasu dengaku, with mirin measured and no sugar

japanese.dinner.yakitori.name: Yakitori (Grilled Chicken & Spring Onion Skewers) with Edamame & Brown Rice
japanese.dinner.yakitori.basedOn: Yakitori, Japanese skewers of chicken and spring onion grilled over charcoal with a soy-mirin tare glaze.
components: Primary: 120 g chicken and spring onion skewers (negima) with soy-mirin glaze, plus shiitake skewers
Shredded cabbage with lemon and sesame
Edamame, 50 g
Small bowl brown rice (45 g uncooked)
steps: Cook the brown rice (45 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).

Trim the chicken thigh of visible fat and cut into 3 cm pieces; cut the spring onion whites into 3 cm lengths. Thread chicken and spring onion alternately on skewers, and the shiitake on a separate skewer.
Simmer the soy, mirin, grated ginger and 2 tablespoons water for 2 minutes to make a light tare.
Grill the skewers under a hot grill or on a griddle pan 4 minutes a side with a pinch of salt; brush with the tare in the last 2 minutes and once more off the heat.
Boil the edamame 4 minutes. Shred the cabbage and toss with lemon juice and toasted sesame seeds.
Serve the cabbage and edamame first, then the skewers, with the small bowl of rice.
japanese.dinner.yakitori.source: Adapted from the traditional yakitori negima, with mirin measured and no sugar in the tare

japanese.dinner.yosenabe.name: Yosenabe (Chicken, Prawn & Tofu Hot Pot) with Small Rice
japanese.dinner.yosenabe.basedOn: Yosenabe, the Japanese 'gather-everything' hot pot of chicken, seafood, tofu and vegetables simmered in dashi at the table.
components: Primary: hot pot of chicken (50 g), prawns (50 g) and tofu (60 g) in dashi-soy
Napa cabbage, shiitake, carrot and daikon from the pot
Lemon and a drizzle of sesame oil
Small bowl brown rice (45 g uncooked)
steps: Cook the brown rice (45 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).
Make 600 ml dashi: soak the kombu 15 minutes, bring to a simmer, remove it, add the bonito flakes, rest 2 minutes and strain. Season with the soy.
Cut the napa cabbage into 4 cm pieces, the carrot and daikon into thin rounds, the tofu into cubes; halve the shiitake. Trim and cube the chicken; peel the prawns.
Simmer the daikon and carrot in the dashi 5 minutes, add the chicken and cabbage stalks for 5 minutes, then the cabbage leaves, shiitake and tofu for 3 minutes.
Add the prawns for the final 2 minutes and finish with spring onion, a squeeze of lemon and the sesame oil.
Eat the vegetables and broth first, then the chicken, prawns and tofu, with the small bowl of rice.

swaps.note: 60 g, add 3 minutes before the end

japanese.lunch.chicken-teriyaki.name: Chicken Teriyaki with Brown Rice & Cucumber Sunomono
japanese.lunch.chicken-teriyaki.basedOn: Tori no teriyaki, chicken glazed in soy and mirin, one of the best-known dishes of Japanese home cooking.
components: Primary: 120 g chicken teriyaki (soy, 1 tsp mirin, ginger, garlic; no sugar)
Cucumber and wakame sunomono (vinegar salad)
French beans and carrot, blanched, with edamame
1 small bowl brown rice (60 g uncooked)
steps: Cook the brown rice (60 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).
Slice the cucumber thinly, salt lightly and squeeze after 5 minutes; soak the wakame 5 minutes, drain, and toss both with the rice vinegar.
Blanch the french beans and carrot batons 3 minutes with the edamame; drain.
Slice the chicken breast into 2 cm strips. Heat the rice bran oil in a non-stick pan and sear the chicken 3 minutes a side until just cooked through.
Add soy, mirin, grated ginger and garlic with 1 tablespoon water; toss 1 minute until the strips are glazed.
Box the rice, vegetables and sunomono with the chicken on top.
japanese.lunch.chicken-teriyaki.source: Adapted from the traditional tori no teriyaki, with mirin measured and no sugar

japanese.lunch.nikujaga.name: Nikujaga (Beef, Potato & Onion Stew) with Brown Rice
components: Primary: nikujaga of 100 g lean beef strips, potato, onion, carrot and french beans in dashi-soy (1 tsp mirin)
Spinach ohitashi with sesame
2/3 bowl brown rice (45 g uncooked; the potato carries the rest)
steps: Cook the brown rice (45 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).
Make 250 ml dashi with the kombu and bonito flakes.
Cut the potato and carrot into 3 cm chunks and the onion into wedges. Heat the oil and brown the beef strips 1 minute, then add the onion and stir 2 minutes.
Add the potato, carrot, dashi, soy and mirin; cover with a lid resting on the food and simmer 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the french beans for the last 4 minutes and finish uncovered so the liquid reduces to a few spoonfuls.
Blanch the spinach 30 seconds, squeeze, cut and toss with the toasted sesame seeds. Box with the rice; nikujaga is a classic bento dish and good at room temperature.
japanese.lunch.nikujaga.source: Adapted from the traditional nikujaga, with mirin measured and no sugar

japanese.lunch.saba-misoni.name: Saba Misoni (Mackerel in Miso) with Brown Rice & Spinach
japanese.lunch.saba-misoni.basedOn: Saba no misoni, mackerel simmered in miso and ginger, a classic of Japanese home cooking and set lunches.
components: Primary: 1 mackerel simmered in miso and ginger with daikon and shiitake
Spinach ohitashi with soy
1 small bowl brown rice (60 g uncooked)
steps: Cook the brown rice (60 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).
Clean the mackerel, cut into two steaks and score the skin. Pour boiling water over the pieces for 10 seconds to tame the oiliness, then drain.
Cut the daikon into 1 cm half-moons; slice the shiitake. Lay them in a wide pan with 200 ml water and julienned ginger and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the mackerel skin up, cover with a lid resting on the fish and simmer 8 minutes.
Loosen the miso in a ladle of the cooking liquid, stir it in and simmer uncovered 5 minutes more until the sauce is glossy and coats the fish.
Blanch the spinach 30 seconds, squeeze, cut and dress with the soy. Serve with the rice; in a lunchbox the misoni is good at room temperature.
japanese.lunch.saba-misoni.source: Adapted from the traditional saba no misoni, without sugar or mirin

japanese.lunch.salmon-edamame-bowl.name: Grilled Salmon Flake Bowl with Edamame & Cucumber
components: Primary: 100 g grilled salmon, flaked, over 1 small bowl brown rice (60 g uncooked)
Edamame, cucumber and carrot with pickled-style ginger
Nori, sesame and soy-vinegar dressing
steps: Cook the brown rice (60 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest) and season while warm with half the rice vinegar.
Salt the salmon lightly and grill or pan-grill in a dry non-stick pan 4 minutes skin side, 2 minutes flesh side; cool and flake, discarding the skin if you prefer.
Boil the edamame 4 minutes. Dice the cucumber, cut the carrot into matchsticks and slice the ginger paper-thin, tossing it in the remaining vinegar.
Mix the soy with 1 teaspoon water for the dressing.
Build the bowl: rice, then the vegetables and edamame in sections, salmon flakes in the middle, shredded nori and toasted sesame on top; pack the dressing separately.
japanese.lunch.salmon-edamame-bowl.source: Inspired by the Japanese sake flake donburi, built as a lunchbox bowl

japanese.lunch.salmon-teriyaki.name: Salmon Teriyaki with Brown Rice & Carrot Gomae
japanese.lunch.salmon-teriyaki.basedOn: Sake no teriyaki, pan-grilled salmon glazed with soy and mirin, a staple of Japanese home cooking and bento boxes.
components: Primary: 110 g salmon teriyaki (soy, 1 tsp mirin, ginger; no sugar)
Spinach and carrot gomae (sesame dressing)
Edamame, 40 g
1 small bowl brown rice (60 g uncooked)
steps: Rinse the brown rice, soak 20 minutes, then cook in 1.5 times its volume of water, covered, 35 minutes; rest 10 minutes.
Blanch the spinach 30 seconds and the carrot matchsticks 2 minutes; squeeze the spinach dry. Toast and crush the sesame seeds, mix with half a teaspoon of soy and toss through the vegetables.
Boil the edamame 4 minutes in salted water, drain.
Pat the salmon dry and pan-grill skin side down in a dry non-stick pan 4 minutes, turn and cook 2 minutes more.
Mix the remaining soy, the mirin and grated ginger with 1 tablespoon water, pour over the salmon and let it bubble and glaze for 1 minute, spooning it over the fish.
Pack the rice, gomae and edamame in separate corners of the box with the salmon on top; it is good at room temperature.
japanese.lunch.salmon-teriyaki.source: Adapted from the traditional sake no teriyaki, with mirin measured and no sugar

japanese.lunch.yakizakana-teishoku.name: Yakizakana Teishoku (Grilled Fish Set with Miso Soup)
japanese.lunch.yakizakana-teishoku.basedOn: Yakizakana teishoku, the Japanese set meal of salt-grilled fish with miso soup, rice, pickles and a vegetable side.
components: Primary: 130 g salt-grilled white fish with lemon
Miso soup with wakame and spring onion
French bean gomaae and edamame
Quick cucumber and daikon pickles
1 small bowl brown rice (60 g uncooked)
steps: Cook the brown rice (60 g rinsed, 1.5 times water, 35 minutes covered, 10 minutes rest).
Slice the cucumber and daikon thinly, toss with a pinch of salt and the rice vinegar and leave to pickle 15 minutes.
Make 200 ml dashi with the kombu and bonito flakes. Add the soaked wakame, loosen the miso into it off the boil and finish with sliced spring onion.
Blanch the french beans and edamame 3 minutes; toss the beans in toasted crushed sesame and the soy.
Salt the fish 10 minutes ahead, pat dry, brush with the oil and grill or pan-fry 3-4 minutes a side until the skin crisps. Serve with a lemon wedge.
Lay out the set: soup and vegetables first, then the fish, then the small bowl of rice.
japanese.lunch.yakizakana-teishoku.source: Adapted from the traditional yakizakana teishoku

japanese.lunch.zaru-soba-tofu.name: Cold Soba Salad with Tofu, Cucumber & Dipping Sauce
japanese.lunch.zaru-soba-tofu.kidNote: Leave the wasabi out of the child's dipping sauce.
japanese.lunch.zaru-soba-tofu.basedOn: Zaru soba, chilled buckwheat noodles served with a dashi-soy dipping sauce (tsuyu), a Japanese summer classic.
components: Primary: 60 g soba noodles (dry), chilled, with 100 g seared tofu
Cucumber, carrot and edamame with nori and sesame
Dashi-soy dipping sauce (tsuyu) with ginger and wasabi, no sugar
steps: Make the dashi: steep the kombu in 150 ml cold water 10 minutes, bring to a simmer, remove the kombu, add the bonito flakes, rest 2 minutes and strain. Stir in the soy, rice vinegar and grated ginger; chill. This is the tsuyu.
Boil the soba 4-5 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water until cool and drain well.
Press the tofu in paper towel, cut into 2 cm cubes and sear in the sesame oil until golden on two sides.
Boil the edamame 4 minutes. Cut the cucumber and carrot into fine matchsticks; slice the spring onion.
Toss the soba with the vegetables and sesame seeds; top with the tofu, shredded nori and spring onion.
Pack the tsuyu in a small pot (wasabi on the side) and pour over the noodles when eating; keep the box cool.

swaps.note: 2 eggs as a thin rolled omelette, sliced

japanese.lunch.zaru-soba-tofu.source: Adapted from the traditional zaru soba, built into a lunchbox salad

japanese.snack.boiled-egg-soy-wasabi.name: Boiled Egg with Soy & Wasabi, Green Tea
components: Primary: 1 boiled egg with a soy-wasabi dip
Cucumber and carrot sticks, 1 sheet roasted nori
Green tea
steps: Boil the egg 9 minutes, cool under the tap, peel and halve.
Stir the wasabi into the soy for a dip; cut the cucumber and carrot into sticks.
Toast the nori sheet 20 seconds in a dry pan and cut into strips to wrap around the egg or vegetables.
Serve with a cup of green tea; leave the wasabi out of the child's dip.
japanese.snack.boiled-egg-soy-wasabi.source: Japanese home snack of yude tamago with wasabi-joyu

japanese.snack.daikon-carrot-pickle-waln.name: Daikon & Carrot Quick Pickle with Walnuts
components: Primary: Namasu-style daikon and carrot quick pickle with ginger and sesame
20 g walnuts
Roasted barley tea (mugicha)
steps: Cut the daikon and carrot into thin matchsticks, toss with the salt and rest 10 minutes; squeeze out the water.
Dress with the rice vinegar and finely grated ginger; scatter with toasted sesame.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan 3 minutes.
Serve the pickle with the walnuts and a glass of barley tea.
japanese.snack.daikon-carrot-pickle-waln.source: Adapted from the traditional namasu, without sugar

japanese.snack.edamame-sea-salt.name: Edamame with Sea Salt & Green Tea
japanese.snack.edamame-sea-salt.basedOn: Shio edamame, boiled young soybeans in the pod with sea salt, Japan's everyday nibble with tea or beer.
components: Primary: 1 cup edamame in the pod (80 g) with sea salt and toasted sesame
Green tea
steps: Boil the edamame pods in salted water 4-5 minutes; drain well.
Toss with a pinch of salt and the toasted sesame while hot.
Serve warm with a cup of green tea; squeeze the beans from the pods to eat.
japanese.snack.edamame-sea-salt.source: Adapted from the traditional shio edamame

japanese.snack.hiyayakko-tofu.name: Hiyayakko Tofu with Ginger-Soy & Barley Tea
japanese.snack.hiyayakko-tofu.basedOn: Hiyayakko, the Japanese chilled tofu topped with grated ginger, spring onion, bonito flakes and soy.
components: Primary: 80 g chilled tofu cubes with grated ginger, spring onion, bonito flakes and soy
Cucumber and wakame on the side with sesame
Roasted barley tea (mugicha)
steps: Drain the tofu on paper towel 5 minutes and cut into cubes; soak the wakame 3 minutes and squeeze.
Top the tofu with finely grated ginger, sliced spring onion and bonito flakes; pour the soy over just before eating.
Slice the cucumber, toss with the wakame and toasted sesame and set beside the tofu.
Serve with a glass of barley tea.

japanese.snack.miso-soup-cup.name: Miso Soup Cup with Tofu & Barley Tea
components: Primary: 1 cup miso soup with tofu, wakame, shiitake and spring onion
Roasted barley tea (mugicha)
steps: Make dashi: steep the kombu in 250 ml water, bring almost to the boil, remove it, add the bonito flakes, rest 2 minutes and strain.
Simmer the sliced shiitake in the dashi 3 minutes; add the cubed tofu and wakame for 2 minutes more.
Off the heat, dissolve the miso through a ladle and add sliced spring onion.
Serve in a cup with a glass of barley tea.
japanese.snack.miso-soup-cup.source: Adapted from the everyday Japanese tofu and wakame miso soup

japanese.snack.roasted-nori-almonds.name: Roasted Nori with Almonds & Green Tea
japanese.snack.roasted-nori-almonds.basedOn: Yaki nori, Japanese roasted seaweed sheets lightly brushed with sesame oil and salt, eaten as a crisp snack.
components: Primary: 2 sheets roasted nori, cut into crisps, with sesame oil and salt
20 g almonds
Green tea
steps: Brush the nori sheets very lightly with the sesame oil and sprinkle with a few grains of salt.
Toast in a dry pan or under the grill 20-30 seconds a side until crisp and fragrant; cut into squares with scissors.
Toast the almonds in the same pan 2 minutes.
Serve the nori crisps and almonds with a cup of green tea.
japanese.snack.roasted-nori-almonds.source: Adapted from the traditional yaki nori

japanese.snack.sunomono-boiled-egg.name: Cucumber Sunomono with Boiled Egg & Barley Tea
japanese.snack.sunomono-boiled-egg.basedOn: Sunomono, the Japanese vinegared cucumber and wakame salad served as a small refreshing side.
components: Primary: Cucumber and wakame sunomono with sesame
1 boiled egg
A small handful of edamame
Roasted barley tea (mugicha)
steps: Boil the egg 9 minutes; drop the edamame in for the last 4 minutes. Cool both under the tap and peel the egg.
Slice the cucumber thinly, salt lightly, rest 5 minutes and squeeze out the water. Soak the wakame 3 minutes and squeeze.
Toss the cucumber and wakame with the rice vinegar, soy, grated ginger and toasted sesame.
Serve with the halved egg, the edamame and a glass of barley tea (hot or chilled).
japanese.snack.sunomono-boiled-egg.source: Adapted from the traditional kyuri no sunomono
